unit.title: Greetings, More Letters, and Simple Words

lesson.title: Continuing the Alphabet: ਛ, ਜ, and ਝ
lesson.subject: punjabi

contentBlocks.text: Last year you learned eleven Gurmukhi letters, ending with ਚ. Today we'll continue right where you left off with three more letters: ਛ, ਜ, and ਝ.

ਛ (chhachha) makes a breathier 'chh' sound, related to yesterday's ਚ. ਜ (jaja) makes a 'j' sound, like in 'jump'. ਝ (jhajha) makes a breathier 'jh' sound, related to ਜ. Practice saying all three: chha... ja... jha. Notice the pattern — just like the ਕ ਖ ਗ ਘ row you learned last year, this row has related sounds too.
You now know fourteen Gurmukhi letters! You're building real reading skills, one letter at a time.

objectives: Recognize and name the letters ਛ (chhachha), ਜ (jaja), and ਝ (jhajha)
Recall all eleven letters learned last year, connecting them to today's three new letters
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review the eleven letters learned last year, ending with ਚ.
2. Introduce ਛ, ਜ, ਝ one at a time, saying each name aloud together three times.
3. Point out the sound-family pattern, just like last year's ਕ ਖ ਗ ਘ ਙ row.
4. Trace each letter in the air before picking up a pencil.
5. Move to the worksheet: trace each letter, then write it once more on the practice line.
6. Close by reciting all fourteen letters learned so far, in order.
differentiationTips: Struggling: if last year's eleven letters aren't fully secure, spend extra time reviewing those before adding new ones
Ready for more: ask the child to guess what letter might come next in this row (a hint: it's a nasal sound, like ਙ was for the previous row)
For a child who enjoys patterns, point out how many Gurmukhi consonant rows follow this same related-sounds structure
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and recognition activity — check that each traced letter roughly matches the shape shown.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Continuing the Painti Akhari sequence from exactly where Kindergarten left off builds directly on prior-year learning, keeping the same systematic, well-established letter-by-letter progression.
